summary: CRISIS regime. March 3 opens with maximum fear: Trump confirmed 25% tariffs on Canada/Mexico effective March 4 (after 1-month delay from Feb 1 announcement), plus China tariffs doubling from 10% to 20%. Consumer confidence posted largest monthly drop since Aug 2021 (Conference Board fell to 98.3, expectations sub-80 recession threshold). Walmart slashed guidance. DOGE mass federal layoffs (62,000+ in Feb alone) creating employment shock. S&P 500 closed Feb 28 at 5,954 after already selling off from Feb 19 all-time high of ~6,144. Gold hit record $2,837. Bitcoin crashed 17.6% in Feb to $84,373. The tariff implementation on March 4 is the immediate catalyst — markets will price in supply chain disruption, input cost inflation, retaliatory tariffs from Canada/Mexico/China, and recession risk. Q1 2025 ended with S&P 500 down ~5%, Nasdaq down ~13%, Consumer Discretionary down 14%, Info Tech down 12.8%. Defensive sectors (Energy +9.3%, Healthcare +6.1%, Staples +4.6%) massively outperformed. On March 3, the S&P 500 shed 1.8% — its biggest one-day decline of the year at that point. March 4 was worse: S&P -2.7%, Nasdaq -4%.

sections.title: Geopolitics
sections.content: Ukraine-Russia: Trump administration pressuring Ukraine hard — Feb Oval Office blowup with Zelenskyy, Hegseth called pre-2014 borders 'unrealistic', US-Russia talks in Saudi Arabia on Feb 18. No ceasefire imminent but peace narrative creates uncertainty for defense spending. China: Tariff escalation from 10% to 20% effective March 4, China retaliating with 15% tariffs on US chicken/wheat/corn/cotton and 10% on soybeans/pork/beef effective March 10. Full trade war escalation underway across 3 largest US trading partners simultaneously. Canada imposing 25% retaliatory tariffs on $21B of US goods. Mexico preparing 5-20% retaliation on pork, cheese, produce, steel.

sections.title: Macro
sections.content: Consumer confidence plunged 7 points to 98.3 in February — largest drop since Aug 2021. Expectations index fell below 80 (recession signal) for first time since June 2024. 12-month inflation expectations surged from 5.2% to 6.0%. Buying conditions for durables collapsed 19%. Fed holding rates steady — inflation still above 2% target but labor market cooling. PPI rose 3.4% YoY. February jobs: 92,000 cuts, unemployment rose to 4.4%. DOGE federal layoffs: 62,530 in Feb, another 216,670 in March — largest monthly job cuts on record. Goldman cut S&P 500 EPS growth forecast from 11% to 9%. Recession probability rising sharply. ISM noted companies experiencing 'operational shocks' from tariff policy with spot commodity prices up ~20%.

sections.title: Corporate
sections.content: Walmart cut FY guidance (3-4% sales growth vs 5% prior), stock fell 6%. Target and Costco fell 2%+ in sympathy. Auto sector bracing for 25% tariffs on Mexican/Canadian supply chains — GM, Ford, Stellantis all heavily exposed. GM imports ~50% of US-sold vehicles from Mexico/South Korea, facing $4-5B in 2025 tariff costs. ADM: crushing profits down 81% in 2025, soybean margins gutted. Challenger job cut announcements surged 245% in February led by government sector. Corporate earnings expectations being revised down across cyclical sectors.

sections.title: TechAI
sections.content: DeepSeek shock from late January still reverberating — Chinese AI startup matched US capabilities at fraction of cost ($5.6M vs billions), wiped $589B from Nvidia in single day. NVDA closed Feb 28 at $124.88, down significantly from Jan highs. Mag 7 under pressure: TSLA -28% in Feb (closed $292.98), AAPL $241.02, MSFT $393.97, AMZN $212.28, META $665.53. Tech sector posted -12.8% in Q1 2025. Semiconductor supply chain faces dual threat: China tariff retaliation + DeepSeek narrative questioning US AI capex premium. AMD at $99.86, QCOM at $152.75, AVGO at $197.23 — all vulnerable to China revenue disruption.

sections.title: Energy
sections.content: WTI crude supported by tight supply — Cushing inventories at decade lows. OECD inventories declining, global inventories fell 49.3 mb in January. US sanctions on Russia/Iran not yet materially impacting supply but creating upside risk. Energy was best-performing sector in Q1 2025 (+9.3%) as defensive/inflation hedge. Natural gas up 40% in 6 months. Canadian energy tariffed at only 10% (lower than 25% on other goods) — creates relative advantage for energy vs other Canadian imports.

sections.title: Policy
sections.content: Triple tariff shock: 25% on Canada/Mexico (March 4) + 20% on China (March 4) + steel/aluminum tariffs coming March 12. DOGE dismantling federal workforce at unprecedented pace — judges blocked some terminations but chaos continues. ISM data shows companies already experiencing 'operational shocks' from tariff policy with spot commodity prices up ~20%. Administration rhetoric shows no signs of backing down. Market pricing in extended trade war, not temporary negotiating tactic. This is the opening salvo — Liberation Day (April 2) with much larger global tariffs still weeks away.

scenarios.trade: GM is the highest-conviction short for March 3. Nearly half its US-sold vehicles are imported from tariffed countries. The cost impact is enormous relative to margins. Consumer confidence collapse means they cannot pass through price increases. Stellantis already announcing plant shutdowns. The S&P 500 fell 1.8% on March 3 (biggest day of 2025 to that point) and then 2.7% on March 4 — auto stocks led both selloffs. Entry at Feb 28 close of $48.51, target $44.50 (8.3% move), stop at $50.00 (3.1% risk). R:R of 2.7:1.

scenarios.implication: Trump announced partial USMCA exemptions within days (March 6), reducing impact. GM could rally on any tariff delay/softening rhetoric. Stock already pricing in some tariff risk from Feb 1 announcement.

scenarios.trade: Ford is more leveraged to the tariff shock than GM due to higher Mexico production concentration and thinner margins. Consumer pullback from confidence collapse hits Ford's core truck/SUV buyer. The combination of tariff cost shock + demand destruction is lethal for a low-margin automaker. Entry at $9.08, target $8.40 (7.5% move), stop at $9.40 (3.5% risk). R:R of 2.1:1.

scenarios.implication: Stock already near historic lows — limited downside. Possible USMCA exemption could spark sharp short squeeze. Ford's domestic production mix may partially offset. Very low share price means small dollar moves are large percentage moves.

scenarios.trade: NVDA is the highest-beta way to express bearish tech/AI/China view simultaneously. The 20% China tariff creates immediate revenue risk. DeepSeek challenged the narrative that only massive US capex can produce frontier AI. In CRISIS regime, highest-momentum names fall hardest. NVDA lost $589B in a single day in January — precedent for violent moves. Entry at $124.88, target $116.00 (7.1% move), stop at $129.00 (3.3% risk). R:R of 2.2:1.

scenarios.implication: NVDA earnings power is real and growing. Positive AI capex news could reverse sentiment. Stock already down significantly from Jan highs. Institutional dip-buying may emerge.

scenarios.trade: Nike sits at the intersection of multiple bearish themes: tariff exposure on Vietnam/Indonesia/China manufacturing, consumer spending pullback, China market weakness, and brand erosion. The March 4 China tariff increase (10% to 20%) directly impacts Nike's supply chain costs. Consumer confidence collapse means discretionary footwear/apparel demand contracts. Entry at $77.08, target $72.00 (6.6% move), stop at $79.50 (3.1% risk). R:R of 2.1:1.

scenarios.implication: Tariffs on Southeast Asia don't hit until Liberation Day (April 2). March 4 tariffs are Canada/Mexico/China — Nike's Vietnam exposure may not be immediately impacted. New CEO turnaround initiatives possible.

scenarios.trade: Target is the weakest link in retail. Unlike Walmart (trade-down beneficiary) and Costco (membership model), Target sits in the middle — too upscale for trade-down, too mass-market for premium. Higher China import exposure than peers. When Walmart cuts guidance, Target's outlook is worse. Entry at $118.78, target $112.00 (5.7% move), stop at $122.50 (3.1% risk). R:R of 1.8:1.

scenarios.implication: Stock already down 6.9% in Feb — some weakness priced in. Target could announce cost-cutting. Possible tariff exemptions on consumer goods. Short interest may be elevated creating squeeze risk.

scenarios.trade: In a tariff-driven selloff, defense is one of the few sectors with positive catalysts. Government defense spending is exempt from DOGE cuts (increasing). Lockheed has zero tariff exposure. Flight-to-quality rotation into defensive sectors with earnings visibility favors LMT. Entry at $435.16, target $450.00 (3.4% move), stop at $425.00 (2.3% risk). R:R of 1.5:1.

scenarios.implication: Broad market selloff could drag all stocks lower regardless of fundamentals. DOGE rhetoric could spook defense investors. Ukraine peace deal would reduce geopolitical premium. Stock already near highs.
